issue.body:
## Context

This issue preserves the dedicated state-preserving upgrade rehearsal from
`v2026.07.23` (`0.2.14`) to `v2026.08.06` (`0.2.15`). It is now backlog rather
than active work.

The current release-candidate program in #49 first converges the existing
network on `v2026.08.06` as an operational prerequisite, then evaluates the
state-preserving update to the `v0.2.16` lab candidate. That preparation does
not constitute a reproducible PASS for this historical transition.

Before this issue resumes, replace any stale command examples with the exact
upgrade interface and profile names from then-current `main`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The run starts from current PASS evidence for an exact `v2026.07.23`
      five-validator baseline.
- [ ] Pre-upgrade evidence records participants, consensus validators and
      voting power, versions, chain progress, and common-height state.
- [ ] The proposal uses the reviewed future activation height, live minimum
      deposit, and immutable `v2026.08.06` profile.
- [ ] Every required chain and API service activates the pinned target.
- [ ] Consensus interruption, Host downtime, and catch-up are measured.
- [ ] Block production resumes and all required Hosts converge.
- [ ] Chain, Genesis, participant, validator, and operator-owned identity are
      preserved.
- [ ] PoC, confirmation-PoC, and authenticated inference complete after the
      upgrade.
- [ ] Partial rollout recovery resumes the same target without reset or
      downgrade.
- [ ] Evidence and the four-state verdict belong to one rehearsal.

## Related work

- #29 – exact historical `v2026.07.23` baseline
- #49 – current release-candidate qualification

issue.body:
## Context

The supported first-time independent Host JOIN guide is now published in
[`ROLE-JOIN.md`](../blob/main/net-deployment-runbook/ROLE-JOIN.md). It uses one
public-bootstrap command and operator-owned state without Genesis private
material.

This M3 issue tracks onboarding material beyond that shipped first-time flow.
It must stay aligned with the interfaces that are actually supported by
current `main` and must not advertise repair or recovery behavior before those
paths are implemented and verified.

## Deliverable

Maintain an external-participant guide that explains:

- Host prerequisites and SSH configuration;
- the default and optional operator data directory;
- public-host and split Network Node/MLNode inputs;
- the canonical `gdc host join ...` command;
- onboarding, effective-validator, and final JOIN acceptance states;
- operator-owned backups and sanitized evidence;
- the verified public Genesis bootstrap and trust boundary;
- separately supported stop, start, verification, repair, restore, and reset
  operations.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every documented command exists on current `main` and has a CLI contract
      test.
- [ ] A new operator can follow the local-GPU and split Network Node/MLNode
      paths without another operator's private state.
- [ ] The guide clearly distinguishes participant activation, effective
      validator membership, and final JOIN acceptance.
- [ ] Unsupported repair or restore behavior is identified as unsupported
      instead of being presented as a workaround.
- [ ] Public-opening criteria use current five-validator chain evidence and
      truthful public observability, not historical deployment state.
- [ ] A future independent operator review records the exact release and
      concrete defects, but it is not a prerequisite for retaining the shipped
      first-time JOIN interface.

## Related work

- #22 – release-specific JOIN timing
- #49 – current release-candidate qualification

issue.body:
## Context

This issue preserves the clean `v2026.07.23` (`0.2.14`) five-validator baseline
rehearsal. It is no longer the active release-qualification path: current work
prepares the existing network on `v2026.08.06` before testing the `v0.2.16`
candidate in #49.

Resume this issue only when an exact `0.2.14` baseline must be reproduced. Do
not use historical topology or a later release as evidence for this scope.

## Canonical flow

```bash
./gdc.sh network reset --yes
./gdc.sh --release v2026.07.23 genesis gdc-node0

# Run from separate operator-owned data directories.
./gdc.sh host join --public-host <dns> gdc-node1
./gdc.sh host join --public-host <dns> gdc-node2
./gdc.sh host join --public-host <dns> gdc-node3
./gdc.sh host join --public-host <dns> gdc-node4 gdc-node4-ml

./gdc.sh --release v2026.07.23 network verify
```

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] The rehearsal starts from an explicit reset and records release/profile,
      chain, Genesis, and separate operator-state identities.
- [ ] Genesis becomes an effective validator and serves authenticated
      inference before additional joins.
- [ ] At least one independent Host JOIN uses only public Genesis inputs and
      produces a chain-verifiable sanitized receipt.
- [x] The chain contains exactly the five expected active participant
      identities.
- [ ] All five validator keys have positive consensus voting power.
- [x] Every Host has a unique runtime and positive accepted PoC weight for the
      selected model.
- [x] The split node4/node4-ml deployment is verified as one participant with
      its linked ML Host.
- [ ] All Network Nodes are caught up within the bounded lag and agree at a
      common height.
- [ ] Confirmation-PoC and authenticated gateway inference complete with
      current-run accounting evidence.
- [ ] The final verdict is `PASS`, `FAIL`, `BLOCKED`, or `INCONCLUSIVE` and
      cannot inherit a historical success.

## Related work

- #30 – historical state-preserving `0.2.14` to `0.2.15` rehearsal
- #49 – current `v0.2.16` and DevShard v5 candidate qualification

body:
Baseline capture is complete. The candidate source heads still match the expected 2026-08-25 laboratory label, so the first profile remains `v2026.08.25-rc.0`.

The repository currently has only the existing read-only runbook workflow and no laboratory-candidate packages. The live DevNet is advancing across all five public Host endpoints, but it is still running the `v2026.07.23` core stack. Validator effectiveness and gateway routability changed across the sampled lifecycle boundary, and the public software-version route currently returns 503, so this is not a proven `v2026.08.06` baseline.

I am freezing the immutable two-source candidate manifest and implementing the candidate lifecycle next. The network will not be updated until reviewed default-branch automation exists and the `v2026.08.06` baseline is verified without resetting lineage.

body:
Correction: all current review findings are corrected together and the exact-head validation cycle is green; the campaign remains `In review` until the unchanged current revision is approved and merged

## Current result

- The OPS Compose model declares a protocol-isolated v5 gateway state volume, and the rendered v5 configuration mounts that volume successfully
- Build manifest verification binds every image and binary entry to its component key, exact candidate tag, publication run identity, archive filename, release URL and OCI repository
- Immutable release locks use an atomic no-clobber claim, so concurrent incompatible writers cannot both succeed
- The candidate definition excludes v5 HA deployment and renders `GONKA_HA=false` with memory storage until a reviewed replica, router and shared-storage lifecycle exists
- Binary OCI tags are stable across partial failed-job reruns because they bind to the profile, definition checksum and immutable publication run ID without the workflow attempt number

## Verification

- Regressions render the v5 Compose configuration, reject swapped manifest entries and cross-component URLs, synchronize incompatible lock writers and verify the disabled HA definition and lock values
- Retry regressions accept unchanged binary references from a later workflow attempt and reject attempt-scoped binary tags
- The complete local gate passes, including the full test suite, ShellCheck, actionlint, release-profile verification, Docker Bats, DinD Bats and a real pinned-Syft binary payload check
- The exact-head GitHub runbook workflow passes and all 27 review threads are resolved

## Authorization boundary

No candidate package has been published, default-branch candidate automation has not been run and the live DevNet has not been changed

Approval of the unchanged current revision by `ever-guild-ops` and an authorized merge into `main` remain required before candidate publication or any network update

## Next action

A fresh review from `ever-guild-ops` is requested; wait for the verdict on the unchanged revision without duplicate requests or routine polling

If the revision changes, repeat the complete exact-head checks and review

After approval and an authorized merge, move the campaign to `In progress` for candidate publication and independent verification, not `Done`

issue.title: Show DevShard version and runtime state on the public site

repository.name: external-test-lab
repository.description: External Test Lab & Community DevNet for the Gonka AI network: public artifacts

issue.body:
## Goal

Show which DevShard protocol the Community DevNet is configured to use and
which versions are actually observed in the running inference fleet.

## Required behavior

- Show the configured Gonka release and DevShard protocol in the network
  summary.
- Show configured and observed DevShard versions as separate values.
- Show active runtime count, routable capacity, and observation freshness.
- Represent a rolling mixed-version state, for example `v4: 2 · v5: 3`.
- Show unavailable, stale, and configuration/runtime mismatch states
  explicitly. A mismatch must not appear as `READY`.
- Derive configured values from immutable profiles and observed values from
  fresh runtime evidence. Do not embed version constants in the page.
- Keep DevShard identity at network and gateway level rather than repeating it
  on every validator card.
- Preserve the normalized desktop and mobile Host-card layout.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The page distinguishes configured and observed DevShard versions.
- [ ] A rolling mixed-version deployment is represented truthfully.
- [ ] Runtime count, routable capacity, and freshness agree with gateway and
      monitoring evidence.
- [ ] Missing or contradictory evidence produces `Unavailable`, `Stale`, or
      `Mismatch`, never a fabricated healthy state.
- [ ] Desktop and mobile browser checks pass without Host-card layout changes.
- [ ] Automated tests cover ready, unavailable, stale, mismatch, and mixed
      version states.

## Related work

- [#49](https://github.com/paranjko/external-test-lab/issues/49) is the
  predecessor qualification campaign. Work starts only after #49 is complete.
- Deliver this work independently in its own focused pull request.

issue.body:
## Context

The Community DevNet is already on the `0.2.15` baseline. The host-scoped
upgrade implementation from #41 is available, but the historical
`0.2.14` to `0.2.15` transition was not executed as an independent five-Host
rehearsal. A current runtime version is not evidence of that procedure.

## Objective

Prove the independent Host upgrade contract end to end on a reproducible
five-Host environment, using a supported source and target release pair. Keep
the result separate from the historical `0.2.14` to `0.2.15` claim.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The immutable upgrade manifest records proposal ID, activation height,
      source and target release profiles, artifact URLs and checksums, chain
      ID, and Genesis SHA-256.
- [ ] Each governance voter signs with only its own operator keyring. No
      aggregated keyring or central SSH controller performs the votes.
- [ ] Each Host operator runs `host upgrade prepare` and `host upgrade watch`
      for its own Host and produces a sanitized `VALIDATOR_EFFECTIVE` receipt.
- [ ] The receipts prove target runtime identity, synchronization, positive
      consensus voting power, and unchanged Host identity.
- [ ] An end-to-end test harness invokes the same host-scoped commands and
      covers interruption and resume against the exact immutable target.
- [ ] The public network verification records one coherent four-state verdict
      for the five-Host rehearsal.

## Scope boundary

This issue does not reclassify the historical `0.2.14` to `0.2.15` rehearsal
as passed. It supplies current, reproducible evidence for the capability
implemented in #41 and complements the historical runtime verdict in #30.

## Related work

- #41 – host-scoped upgrade implementation.
- #30 – historical `0.2.14` to `0.2.15` runtime rehearsal.
- #49 – current release qualification.

issue.title: fix: read probe millisecond clocks from EPOCHREALTIME

labels.name: wontfix
labels.description: This will not be worked on

repository.name: external-test-lab
repository.description: External Test Lab & Community DevNet for the Gonka AI network: public artifacts

issue.body:
## Scope

This PR is **not** a solution for issue #49. It fixes one defect found on the way: the public gateway health document and the DevNet RPC helper can report wrong millisecond latencies, and request deadlines use the wrong unit. The #49 work that remains (owner-authorized `gdc ops site` / `gdc ops edge`, public inference acceptance, the DevShard v5 rollout, and the Gonka v0.2.16 transition) needs owner-held credentials and live infrastructure. This PR does not attempt any of it.

Part of #49.

## Defect and root cause

`https://gonka-dev.net/status/gateway-health` currently reports values like `"latency_ms": 19651863` and `23603745` for a probe that runs every few seconds.

The affected scripts took millisecond timestamps with `date +%s%3N`. Ubuntu 26.04, a supported Host OS, ships uutils coreutils 0.8.0 as `date`, and that `date` ignores the `%3N` width and prints unpadded nanoseconds:

| `date` implementation | `date +%s%3N` |
|---|---|
| GNU coreutils 9.1 / 9.4 | `1790273287205` (correct) |
| uutils 0.3.0 – 0.6.0 | 13 digits (correct) |
| uutils 0.7.0 | `1790273355137920493` |
| uutils 0.8.0 (stock `ubuntu:26.04` image) | `1790274278470608404` |
| uutils 0.9.0 – 0.12.0 | 13 digits (correct) |

These values were checked on 2026-09-24 with the upstream uutils release binaries and the `ubuntu:26.04` container. Because the output is unpadded, the difference between two readings is in nanoseconds, or garbage when the digit counts differ. Fed the uutils-0.7 behaviour, the unmodified `main` probe published `latency_ms: -1611246130079893093`.

## Change

- Every `date +%s%3N` in `04-ops/`, `scripts/`, and `devnet/node_scripts/find_best_rpc.sh` becomes `$(( ${EPOCHREALTIME//[!0-9]/} / 1000 ))`, the bash ≥ 5.0 builtin. Bash 5.3 on Ubuntu 26.04 and bash 5.1/5.2 on 22.04/24.04 provide it, and these scripts already need bash 4 features (`declare -A`, `mapfile`). No `date` subprocess, no shared helper file, and nothing new for `install-ops.sh` to deploy. This replaces the two copies of `epoch-millis.sh` from the earlier revision.
- The readiness waiter rejects a `completion_finished_ms` later than now + 1 s, so a probe host that still produces nanosecond receipts can't pass for fresh.
- The public health schema checks in `verify-public-homepage.sh` and `capture-gateway-observability.sh` bound `latency_ms` to `[0, 60000]` and require a 13-digit `completion_finished_ms` when it isn't zero.

## Tests

- `scripts/test-gateway-health-probe.sh` runs the real probe with a `date` on `PATH` that behaves like uutils 0.7/0.8, and asserts `latency_ms` is in `[0, 60000]` and `completion_finished_ms` has 13 digits. It fails against the `main` probe and passes on this branch.
- `scripts/test-public-traffic-readiness.sh` adds a nanosecond-scale future receipt, which must be rejected.
- `scripts/test-profiles.sh` fails if any `$(date …%3N)` comes back into `04-ops/` or `scripts/`.
- `devnet/node_scripts/test-find_best_rpc.sh` mocks uutils-style nanoseconds and RPC responses, then checks the reported latency is in milliseconds. It fails before this fix and passes afterward. The runbook workflow runs it on changes to either DevNet RPC file.
- Locally, `make shellcheck` (ShellCheck v0.11.0), the focused runbook tests above, and all 29 scripts after JOIN preflight pass. The new probe regression fails against unmodified `main` and passes on this branch.
- A full `make test` run from this `/tmp` checkout stops at `test-recovery-contract`: its persistent-output fixture rejects a world-writable parent. The same four assertions fail on unmodified `main`; that test passes from a `/home/box` worktree. With it skipped, the suite stops at the existing `test-join-preflight-diagnostics.sh` five-second observation deadline. The same test fails on `main` in this environment; a local run with a 15-second observation window passes all its assertions. No production deadline was changed.
- The exact-head runbook CI job is `action_required` with no jobs or logs. It still needs maintainer approval for this fork PR.

## Deployment status

Nothing is deployed by this PR. The live probe keeps reporting nanosecond latencies until an owner-authorized OPS reinstall puts the updated `gateway-health-probe.sh` on the gateway Host.



Fixes paranjko/external-test-lab#49
